title: Exact versions, rendered revisions and the cold-definition barrier
summary: Wire UI correctness is fenced by exact definition identities and monotonically increasing view revisions. A CREATE_INSTANCE that references an authorised but not-yet-downloaded immutable definition waits behind a definition barrier rather than forcing a false resync.
invariants: Definitions are addressed by exact definitionId@version; there is no implicit latest resolution.
Every semantic UI action carries the rendered revision against which the user acted.
Stale actions are detected server-side and never silently treated as current actions.
A genuine revision gap causes resynchronisation.
Cold-cache definition latency is not a revision gap: ordered patches wait behind the missing-definition barrier and replay after exact definition installation.
Snapshots are deterministic parent-before-child so a direct renderer can reconstruct state without table-iteration assumptions.

provenance.claim: Dynamic CREATE_INSTANCE and immutable-definition barrier contract.
Renderer manifest, cache-miss validation and deterministic parent-before-child snapshot.
Reconciled cold-cache handling queues CREATE_INSTANCE behind missing immutable definitions.
